_comment: Autarkia's appearance vocabulary. Anima ships the machinery that reads this; everything here
is content. Edit it with tools/appearance-preview (scripts/appearance-preview.sh), which reads
this exact file and runs the exact compositor the game runs.
Ramp shades are fixed point: [hue tenths of a degree, saturation thousandths, value thousandths],
deepest shade first. A ramp replaces one authored colour per shade, and it is written one of two
ways. A bare ARRAY of shades means the art is drawn in the reserved index colours FF0000, FF0001,
FF0002, ... (see Shades) — the right default for art authored from scratch. An OBJECT may add
'keys': the real colours the art is actually drawn in, one per shade, deepest first. That is what
lets a layer be painted in visible colour and still recolour per agent, and it is why 'hair' is
spelled that way — its art is Steve's hair, kept in Steve's own browns.
Either way, a pixel that is neither transparent nor one of that ramp's keys is left exactly as
authored, on purpose, so a stray colour stays visible instead of quietly becoming a shade nobody
chose. Keys must be distinct, and a ramp's keys are part of what its NAME means — two ramps with
the same name and different keys would collide in the bake cache.
A slot marked 'optional' is allowed to draw nothing — a beard, blood, grime. Without it the
editor would rightly complain that a selector with no '*' rule leaves the slot empty for some
combination of parameters, which for these slots is the entire point.
A slot whose selector reads a parameter that changes many times a second MUST be 'dynamic',
or every change re-bakes the shared static base that the whole split exists to protect. The
beard reads 'speaking', so it is dynamic even though a beard itself does not come and go.
